$comment: Character sets referenced by the utility specs, written out as explicit code points. Regex shorthands are deliberately avoided: `\s` means 6 ASCII characters in Go and Ruby, the 25 code points below in JavaScript, and a Unicode property in Python and the Rust regex crate, so a spec that shipped a regex literal would not describe one behaviour. `\d` diverges the same way (Python's `\d` matches Devanagari digits with `re.UNICODE`).

ascii-digits.description: The 10 ASCII digits. This is what every Brazilian document number is made of.

js-whitespace.description: The code points JavaScript's String.prototype.trim() strips and its regex `\s` matches: WhiteSpace plus LineTerminator plus U+FEFF.

mask-cpf.description: Separators accepted between the digit groups of a CPF.

mask-pis.description: Separators accepted anywhere in a PIS/NIS.
